operator_io_quirks: Table/column names are mixed case ('Grape','Appelation','isAVA','No','ID'); must double-quote and preserve original spelling.
Note the misspelling 'Appelation' (one 'l') in both appellations and wine — FK parent_col matches child col exactly, so no dangling FK, but any name-normalisation would break it.
wine has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there, and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to act on.

grapes.Grape and appellations.Appelation are TEXT UNIQUE (line-based 'unique' rule fires); wine.Grape/wine.Appelation are FK children to those unique parents — parent values are unique so FK draw is 1:1, no fan-out.
wine.Cases has storage classes ['integer','text'] — mixed affinity; declared INTEGER but some rows store text. Number fuzzer will emit ints; inserts may coerce or fail.
wine.Year declared INTEGER but semantically a year (2005-2009); ts dispatches to Number (not Date) because type string is 'INTEGER' — no date template.
wine.Drink is TEXT holding mixed 'now' and year strings ('2012','2010') — String fuzzer, no date semantics.
appellations.County and Area contain literal 'N/A' strings (not NULL) — null_rate 0.0 everywhere; no NULLs in original.
appellations.State and wine.State are constant 'California' (distinct=1) — String fuzzer will still emit random strings, destroying the constant.
All tables small (20/57/500 rows) — no huge-table sampling concern; original_values fully read.
No composite keys, no self-references, no dangling FKs, no views/triggers/indexes beyond the UNIQUE constraints.
wine.No is INTEGER distinct=500 but NOT a PK — looks like a surrogate id; ts treats it as plain Number.
operator_ts_expectations: grapes.ID, appellations.No: single-column INTEGER PK -> Number fuzzer, max_l0=inf (unlimited fresh draws), int perturbation +-1/+-2; PK dedup keeps first occurrence.

grapes.Grape, appellations.Appelation: String fuzzer over charset a-zA-Z 0-9() with 0.5 contaminate; UNIQUE constraint means duplicate rows fail at insert and are dropped — likely shrinks these tables.
wine.Grape, wine.Appelation: FK children draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> many duplicate wine rows share a grape/appellation; fine (no unique on wine).

wine.Year/Price/Score/Cases: Number fuzzer, range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (none -> default), so values like 2008 become random ints in a wide range — implausible years/prices/scores drive FN on range predicates (e.g. Year BETWEEN 2005 AND 2010, Score>90).
wine.Drink: String fuzzer emits random strings, never 'now'/year-like — queries filtering Drink='now' or Drink LIKE '20%' get empty/random results -> FN.
appellations.State / wine.State constant 'California' destroyed by String fuzzer -> queries WHERE State='California' return random rows -> FN/FP.
appellations.isAVA ('Yes'/'No') and grapes.Color ('Red'/'White') are 2-value enums; String fuzzer emits arbitrary strings -> equality predicates on these become near-empty -> FN.
wine has no PK: no dedup, so 500 rows all survive; joins wine->grapes/appellations are many-to-one, ties present (good for COUNT/GROUP BY).
appellations.County/Area 'N/A' sentinel: String fuzzer never reproduces 'N/A' -> queries excluding or matching 'N/A' misbehave.
Number fuzzer's list_max quirk (upper end overwritten to full range) means even with original elements present, fresh draws dominate when p small — implausible magnitudes.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit columns at all — those fuzzers never fire on wine_1.
FK consistency holds (parent values reused), so join cardinality is preserved; misses are value-plausibility (FN) and lost constants/enums (FP on negation, FN on equality).
